html:
Franklin D. Roosevelt, known as FDR, was president of the United States from 1933 until his death in 1945. He was elected four times, more than any other president, and led the country through the Great Depression and most of the Second World War.

Born into a rich New York family and a cousin of President Theodore Roosevelt, he studied at Harvard and went into Democratic politics. In 1921 polio left him unable to walk without help, a fact he largely hid from the public. He became governor of New York in 1929.

He won the presidency in 1932, three years after the Wall Street crash, with a quarter of American workers unemployed. His New Deal brought a burst of new programmes:

  • bank reform and deposit insurance to stop bank runs;
  • public works that employed millions, building roads, dams and schools;
  • Social Security, for pensions and unemployment benefits;
  • rights for labour unions.

He spoke to Americans directly over the radio in his "fireside chats". The New Deal greatly enlarged the federal government, and critics said it went too far.

When war broke out in Europe, he helped Britain with Lend-Lease before the US entered the war after the attack on Pearl Harbor in December 1941. He worked with Winston Churchill and Joseph Stalin, approved the Manhattan Project, and backed plans for the post-war order, including Bretton Woods and the United Nations. He died in April 1945, weeks before Germany surrendered. His wartime orders also sent Japanese Americans to internment camps, a decision now seen as a grave wrong.
